# Sofabird

> Free, open-source (GPL-3.0) Android remote control for VLC media player running on a Windows PC or laptop connected
> to a TV, together with its Windows companion app (Sofabird for Windows, required) that turns the PC into a media
> station: a movie and series library with posters, "continue watching", automatic discovery and a Bluetooth fallback
> when Wi-Fi is down; it also plays YouTube videos shared from the phone fullscreen on the TV and starts/ends Moonlight
> game streams. Formerly called VLC Remote (github.com/lex019020/vlc-remote, which redirects here).

Use it when someone wants to control VLC on a Windows PC/HTPC from an Android phone like a TV remote, wants a
Plex/Kodi-like library and resume experience on top of VLC without a media server, or needs a VLC remote that
keeps working without Wi-Fi, or wants to send a YouTube video from the phone to the TV PC and control it from the
phone.

## What it does

- Playback control: play/pause, seek (±10/30 s, hold to repeat, scrub bar with chapters), volume, phone volume keys,
  audio and subtitle tracks with languages, audio/subtitle delay, speed, aspect ratio, fullscreen, playlist.
- Library: browse the PC's drives and network shares; movies and series from the chosen media folders as a poster grid
  with TMDB metadata (title, year, rating, description, backdrops, episode names); network media folders are not
  polled (their computer can sleep) and an unreachable one is named on the phone.
- Watch history: resume prompt ("continue from 37:27?"), next-episode offer, watched marks, per-folder audio and
  subtitle choice for series; YouTube videos played on the TV are in the history and "Continue watching" and open
  where they stopped.
- Sleep timer: pause the TV after a while or at the end of the episode or video, optionally putting the PC to sleep.
- Home screen: when nothing plays, the remote opens on "What shall we watch?" — continue watching (TMDB stills,
  YouTube thumbnails), the library, YouTube and another PC's screen (Moonlight).
- Companion (Windows tray app): pairing with a 6-digit code shown on the TV (the connection is then encrypted with
  TLS, the PC's certificate pinned), starts VLC fullscreen on the TV monitor,
  audio output device switching, system volume, screen off, sleep and Wake-on-LAN from the phone, keep-awake during playback, "media station" power
  plan (lid closed, no sleep, survives the TV being turned off), firewall setup with one UAC prompt, quiet automatic
  updates.
- YouTube on the TV: "Share → Sofabird" from the YouTube app or a pasted link opens the video fullscreen in Firefox
  (a TV profile of its own, signed in once) on the TV; a Sofabird extension in that browser gives exact seeking,
  fullscreen after ads, "Skip ad", subtitles and quality; the remote, notification, lock screen and volume keys
  control it; optional ad
  blocking with uBlock Origin and sponsor skipping with SponsorBlock; the companion's setup window installs Firefox.
- One TV screen: the display chosen for the TV is used by VLC, YouTube and Moonlight alike.
- Moonlight: start and end a stream of another computer (Sunshine host) on the TV from the phone, choosing the computer
  and the app (desktop, Steam Big Picture, a game; the app list can be refreshed from the computers, the last choice is
  remembered); during the stream the phone is that computer's touchpad and keyboard, with Moonlight's stats overlay and
  mouse mode as buttons.
- Touchpad and keyboard: the phone moves the PC's pointer (tap to click, two fingers to scroll or right-click, hold to
  drag) and types on it live in any language, with Esc / Tab / Win / arrow keys — for signing in, searching or a
  streamed desktop.
- Works in English and Russian (follows the system language).

## How it compares

- Typical VLC remote apps talk to VLC's web interface directly and need it set up by hand with a password; this app
  works through its companion on the PC instead (since 0.5 it has no direct mode), which configures VLC itself and
  adds discovery, pairing with a code, push updates, a poster library, watch history and Bluetooth.
- Unlike Kodi/Plex/Jellyfin it needs no media server or transcoding: VLC plays the files directly on the PC.

## Install

- Windows: run `Sofabird-Setup.exe` from https://github.com/lex019020/sofabird/releases/latest
  (per-user install, updates itself). Movies play in VLC 3.0.x: when it is missing, the setup window installs it from
  videolan.org. The phone app works only with it.
- Android 8+: install `Sofabird-<version>.apk` from the same release (later updates are offered by the app itself).
  Open the app, pick the PC, type the code shown on the TV.

## Links

- Source and docs: https://github.com/lex019020/sofabird
- Website: https://sofabird.app/
- Protocol (phone ↔ companion): https://github.com/lex019020/sofabird/blob/main/protocol/README.md
- Tech: Kotlin + Jetpack Compose (Android), .NET 10 WinForms + Kestrel (Windows), Velopack installer.
